rows.text: A train horn sounds, followed by a train passing by. The train horn and passing train are audible in the background.

A loud, high-pitched, sustained electronic tone sounds, followed by a brief, low-pitched musical chord. The electronic tone is clearly audible and distinct from the background, while the musical chord is softer and less prominent, occurring after the initial tone.

A loud, sustained musical note plays as the rabbit stands near a cave entrance. The musical note is audible at 2 seconds, coinciding with the rabbit's position near the cave entrance shown in the images.

A sharp, high-pitched click is heard, followed by a brief, low-frequency thump. The click is consistent with a small, hard object being struck or dropped onto a solid surface, while the thump suggests a soft impact or settling of the object.

A soft thud is heard as a heavy object lands on grass. The sound occurs at the same moment a large white rabbit is shown in a grassy field, suggesting the rabbit may have dropped or landed on the ground.

A soft thud is heard as the rabbit's hand makes contact with the apple. The audio captures a gentle impact sound at the moment the rabbit's hand touches the apple, visible in the sequence where the rabbit's hand moves toward and then grasps the apple.
rows.manual_interpretation: False sound assertion on digital-zero PCM; the described rabbit/apple action is visual context, not audible evidence.

findings: Frames helped produce visible source/location claims, not a demonstrated acoustic accuracy gain.
One completed mute control asserted a thud despite all-zero audio; the other mute request was capacity-blocked.
The second normal three-frame request was also blocked; do not score missing pairs as accuracy failures.
RMS candidates establish activity changes, not event identity or perceptual boundaries.
Post-generation reference overlap is incomplete editorial evidence, not independent listening ground truth.
limits: Main-session manual interpretation; tiny two-candidate comparison; no independent listening or DHH evaluation.
